name: e-NAM (National Agriculture Market)
description: A pan-India electronic trading portal which networks the existing APMC mandis to create a unified national market for agricultural commodities.
authority: Small Farmers Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
eligibility: Farmers, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Traders, and Commission Agents registered in APMC mandis
Sellers must have agricultural produce listed in the traded commodities list
benefits: Transparent online trading with better price discovery for farmers
Access to a larger national market beyond local APMC boundaries
Real-time information on commodity prices and arrivals
Direct online payment to farmers' bank accounts
documents: Aadhaar Card or Valid ID Proof

procedure: Visit the e-NAM portal or download the e-NAM mobile app
Select 'Registration Type' (Farmer, Trader, FPO, etc.)
Fill out personal and bank details and submit for registration
Upon approval by the respective APMC, login credentials are provided
Bring produce to the mandi for assaying, weighing, and electronic bidding

name: Kisan Call Centre (KCC)
description: A toll-free expert advisory helpline service available in 22 local languages to answer farmers' queries on agriculture and allied sectors.
authority: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
eligibility: Any farmer or citizen of India seeking agricultural, horticultural, or veterinary advice
benefits: Free access to agricultural experts via toll-free number 1800-180-1551
Information on crop cultivation, disease control, weather forecasts, and market prices
Available from 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM on all 365 days of the year
Escalation to Subject Matter Specialists (SMS) for complex queries

procedure: Dial the toll-free number 1800-180-1551 from any landline or mobile network
Select the preferred local language through the IVR system
Speak directly with the Farm Tele Advisor (FTA) to get solutions

name: Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM)
description: A centrally sponsored scheme promoting custom hiring centers and providing subsidies to farmers for purchasing agricultural machinery and equipment.
authority: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
eligibility: Individual farmers, SHGs, FPOs, and Cooperative Societies
Applicants must own cultivable land and have a valid Aadhaar card
Registered rural entrepreneurs setting up Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs)
benefits: Subsidy ranging from 40% to 50% for individual farmers purchasing tractors, power tillers, and specialized equipment
Up to 80% subsidy for setting up Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs) by farmer groups/FPOs
Financial assistance for high-tech, high-value machinery like drone tech (up to 100% for ICAR/KVKs, 50% for SC/ST/Women/Small farmers, 40% for others)
documents: Right of Record (RoR) / Land ownership documents
Quotation of the machinery from an empanelled manufacturer/dealer

procedure: Register as a farmer on the Direct Benefit Transfer in Agricultural Mechanization Portal (agrimachinery.nic.in)
Select the required machinery and an empanelled vendor
Upload the required land and identity documents
Wait for the approval from the District Agriculture Officer
Pay the farmer's share to the vendor; the subsidy is transferred via DBT or directly to the vendor based on state rules

name: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)
description: An initiative to promote organic farming through a cluster approach and Participatory Guarantee System (PGS) certification.
authority: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
eligibility: Farmers willing to transition to organic farming
Must form a cluster or group of 20 or more farmers having 20 hectares of contiguous land
Small and marginal farmers are given preference
benefits: Financial assistance of ₹50,000 per hectare for a 3-year period
₹31,000 out of ₹50,000 provided directly via DBT to farmers for organic inputs (seeds, bio-fertilizers, bio-pesticides)
Free organic certification through the PGS-India system
Support for capacity building, value addition, and marketing

procedure: Farmers must approach the Local/District Agriculture Department or Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK)
Form a cluster of minimum 20 hectares with neighboring farmers
Register the cluster under the PKVY scheme through the State Nodal Agency
Undergo training and implement organic practices
Receive input subsidy directly in the bank account via DBT over 3 years

verification.notes: Verified from Ministry of Agriculture PKVY operational guidelines.

name: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH)
description: A centrally sponsored scheme for the holistic growth of the horticulture sector encompassing fruits, vegetables, root and tuber crops, mushrooms, spices, flowers, aromatic plants, coconut, cashew, and cocoa.
authority: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
eligibility: Farmers, FPOs, FPCs, Self Help Groups, and NGOs
Agri-entrepreneurs and state horticulture farms
Must own or lease cultivable land suitable for horticulture
benefits: Subsidy ranging from 35% to 50% for establishing new gardens, greenhouses, poly-houses, and shade net houses
Financial assistance for micro-irrigation, mechanization, and cold chain infrastructure (cold storages, pack houses)
Support for mushroom cultivation, beekeeping, and organic farming integration
Quality planting material provision
documents: Land Records (7/12, Khatauni) or Lease Agreement
Detailed Project Report (DPR) for post-harvest infrastructure/greenhouses
Soil/Water test reports (if required by state)

procedure: Visit the District Horticulture Office to understand state-specific annual action plans
Submit the application form along with land documents and the DPR (for large projects) physically or via the state's agriculture portal
The District Level Committee inspects the site and gives administrative approval
Upon completion of the work (e.g., polyhouse construction), joint inspection is conducted
Subsidy is credited via DBT

name: Agmarknet Portal
description: A government portal providing daily market information (arrivals and prices) for agricultural commodities across wholesale APMC markets in India.
authority: Directorate of Marketing & Inspection (DMI)
eligibility: Open to all citizens, farmers, traders, researchers, and policymakers
benefits: Access to daily, weekly, and monthly wholesale price trends of crops
Arrival volume data across thousands of mandis nationwide
Helps farmers make informed decisions about when and where to sell their produce
Free access to market intelligence reports

procedure: Visit the portal https://agmarknet.gov.in
Select the commodity, state, and specific market (mandi)
Select the date range to view minimum, maximum, and modal prices
No login required for viewing basic market reports

name: mKisan SMS Portal
description: An SMS portal enabling Central and State government organizations in agriculture to provide quick, timely, and targeted advisories to farmers.
authority: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
eligibility: Any farmer possessing a mobile phone (feature phone or smartphone)
benefits: Free text and voice message advisories on crop management, weather alerts, pest attacks, and market prices
Advisories are sent in the local language
Pull SMS services available to query specific agricultural information

procedure: Farmers can register via the web portal mkisan.gov.in by providing their mobile number, state, district, block, and crops grown
Alternatively, farmers can register by calling the Kisan Call Centre (1800-180-1551)
Registration can also be done via USSD by dialing *561*11#
Once registered, the farmer automatically receives seasonal advisory SMS

name: National Beekeeping & Honey Mission (NBHM)
description: A central sector scheme promoting scientific beekeeping and production of honey and other beehive products to increase farmers' income.
authority: National Bee Board (NBB) / Ministry of Agriculture
eligibility: Individual farmers, Beekeepers, FPOs, and SHGs
Must be registered with the National Bee Board (NBB) on the Madhukranti portal
benefits: Financial assistance for purchasing bee colonies, hives, and beekeeping equipment
Support for setting up honey processing units, testing labs, and cold storages
Capacity building and training in scientific beekeeping
Enhances crop yield through cross-pollination

procedure: Register on the Madhukranti Portal (madhukranti.in) to get an NBB ID
Submit the application for subsidy/equipment under NBHM through the portal or District Horticulture Office
Undergo basic beekeeping training provided by KVKs/State Departments
Receive the subsidized items or financial grant via DBT

name: Seednet India Portal
description: A national portal for seed lifecycle management, providing information on seed availability, certified seed varieties, and seed dealer networks.
authority: Seed Division, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
eligibility: Farmers seeking quality seeds, Seed Dealers, and Seed Producing Agencies
benefits: Provides real-time information on the availability of Breeder, Foundation, and Certified seeds across states
Database of notified crop varieties suitable for different agro-climatic zones
Verification of seed authenticity through traceability barcodes
List of registered seed dealers and testing laboratories

procedure: Visit seednet.gov.in
Use the 'Seed Availability' dashboard to search for specific crops and varieties in your state
Find contact details of the nearest authorized seed distribution center or State Seed Corporation
Purchase seeds offline using the information gathered

name: INCOIS Potential Fishing Zone (PFZ) Advisories
description: A satellite-based advisory service providing precise locations of fish aggregations to fishermen, reducing search time and fuel cost.
authority: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS)
eligibility: Marine fishermen, Fishing communities, and Trawler operators in India's coastal regions
benefits: Identifies productive fishing zones based on Sea Surface Temperature (SST) and Chlorophyll data
Reduces search time by up to 60-70%, significantly cutting down diesel costs
Increases catch yield and profitability
Provides Ocean State Forecasts (OSF) including wave height and high wind alerts for safety

procedure: Fishermen can view daily PFZ maps on the INCOIS website or the 'Fisher Friend' mobile app
Register mobile numbers via local fisheries cooperatives or NGOs (like MSSRF) to receive direct SMS advisories
PFZ advisories are also broadcast via Electronic Display Boards at major fishing harbours and local radio stations

name: E-Pashuhaat Portal
description: A web portal connecting breeders, state agencies, and farmers to provide information on the availability of disease-free bovine germplasm (semen, embryos, live animals).
authority: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying
eligibility: Dairy farmers, animal breeders, semen stations, and state animal husbandry departments
benefits: Acts as a single platform for buying and selling high-yielding, disease-free germplasm
Eliminates middlemen, ensuring fair prices for breeders and quality for buyers
Provides complete traceability of genetic material
Access to information on artificial insemination services and progeny-tested bulls

procedure: Visit the e-Pashuhaat portal
Search for semen doses, embryos, or live animals by breed, state, and yielding capacity
Register as a buyer to contact the registered breeder or semen station
Transact securely based on verified genetic merits listed on the portal

name: PGS-India (Participatory Guarantee System)
description: A decentralized organic farming certification system built on trust and peer review among farmers, making certification affordable and accessible for domestic markets.
authority: National Centre of Organic Farming (NCOF)
eligibility: Farmers practicing organic agriculture
Must form a local group (minimum 5 farmers) residing in the same or nearby villages
Farmers must pledge to follow the National Standards for Organic Production (NSOP)
benefits: Low-cost or free alternative to third-party organic certification
Empowers farmers through peer inspections and shared responsibility
Provides the 'PGS-India Green' (under conversion) or 'PGS-India Organic' (fully organic) logo for marketing
Enhances domestic marketability and price realization for organic produce

procedure: Farmers form a local group and select a lead farmer
The group registers on the PGS-India portal via a Regional Council (RC)
Members conduct peer appraisals of each other's farms periodically
The peer review data is uploaded to the portal
After the conversion period, the RC grants the certification and prints the barcode-enabled PGS logo

name: National Animal Disease Control Programme (NADCP)
description: A central sector scheme aiming for the total eradication of Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) and Brucellosis in livestock through 100% vaccination.
authority: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying
eligibility: All livestock owners (cattle, buffalo, sheep, goat, and pig owners)
Livestock must be ear-tagged and registered on the INAPH database
benefits: 100% free vaccination for FMD for cattle, buffaloes, sheep, goats, and pigs
Free Brucellosis vaccination for 100% of bovine female calves (4-8 months of age)
Reduces milk yield losses and prevents livestock morbidity
Improves the domestic and export marketability of livestock products
documents: Aadhaar Card of the livestock owner
Pashu Aadhaar (12-digit ear tag) for the animal

procedure: The programme is executed via state veterinary departments in campaign modes
Livestock owners must present their animals during village-level vaccination camps
Veterinary workers attach an ear tag (Pashu Aadhaar) to the animal if not already tagged
Vaccination details are uploaded to the Information Network for Animal Productivity and Health (INAPH) portal
A vaccination certificate/health card is issued to the owner

officialSources.sourceName: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying

name: National Livestock Mission (NLM)
description: A mission aiming at sustainable development of the livestock sector focusing on entrepreneurship development in poultry, sheep, goat, and piggery, and fodder development.
authority: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying
eligibility: Individuals, FPOs, SHGs, Section 8 companies, and joint liability groups
Must have suitable land for establishing the farm/infrastructure
Must have arranged bank finance or have own financial capacity for the margin money
benefits: 50% capital subsidy (up to ₹50 Lakh) for establishing rural poultry farms (breeder farms, hatcheries)
50% capital subsidy (up to ₹50 Lakh) for sheep/goat breeding farms (minimum 500 females + 25 males)
50% capital subsidy (up to ₹30 Lakh) for pig breeding farms
50% subsidy (up to ₹50 Lakh) for fodder seed multiplication and fodder block making units
documents: Bank Loan Sanction letter or proof of margin money

procedure: Register on the NLM Entrepreneurship portal (nlm.udyamimitra.in)
Fill out the online application and upload the DPR and land documents
Select the lending bank for loan assessment
The application is screened by the State Implementing Agency (SIA)
Upon bank sanction and SIA recommendation, the Central Government releases the subsidy in installments

name: Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY-RAFTAAR)
description: Remunerative Approaches for Agriculture and Allied Sectors Rejuvenation. The scheme promotes infrastructure development, value addition, and supports agri-startups through incubation.
authority: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
eligibility: States (for infrastructure projects)
Agri-Entrepreneurs and Startups (for innovation and incubation support)
FPOs and Farmer Groups
benefits: Creation of pre-harvest and post-harvest agriculture infrastructure
Agri-entrepreneurship orientation program provides a stipend of ₹10,000 per month for 2 months
Seed stage funding as grant-in-aid up to ₹5 Lakhs for startups
Agri-Business Incubation program offers grant-in-aid up to ₹25 Lakhs for scaling up innovations

procedure: Infrastructure projects are proposed by State Governments in their State Level Sanctioning Committee (SLSC)
For Agri-Startups, candidates must apply to designated RKVY-RAFTAAR Agribusiness Incubators (R-ABIs) across the country (like IARI, MANAGE, TNAU)
Submit a business proposal online or via email to the R-ABI during application calls
Present the pitch to the selection committee for grant approval

name: National Bamboo Mission (NBM)
description: Scheme to increase the area under bamboo plantation in non-forest lands and to promote product development and market linkage for bamboo.
authority: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
eligibility: Farmers, Artisans, Entrepreneurs, and State Government Agencies
Must own land suitable for bamboo cultivation
benefits: Financial assistance of ₹50,000 per hectare for bamboo cultivation (distributed over 3 years)
Subsidy (up to 50%) for setting up bamboo nurseries
Assistance for establishing primary processing units, treatment plants, and product development centers
Exemption of Indian-grown bamboo on non-forest lands from the definition of 'tree' under the Indian Forest Act, allowing free movement

procedure: Contact the District Horticulture Officer, District Forest Officer, or State Bamboo Mission nodal officer
Submit the application with land records for plantation subsidy
Procure certified saplings from approved nurseries
Plantation is physically verified before DBT release of the subsidy in a 50:30:20 ratio over three years

name: iKhedut Portal
description: An integrated state agriculture portal by the Government of Gujarat allowing farmers to apply for multiple state and central agricultural subsidies online.
authority: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Co-operation Department, Govt. of Gujarat
eligibility: Farmers domiciled in Gujarat
Must hold agricultural land in the state
Must have a bank account
benefits: Single-window online application for subsidies on tractors, farm implements, tarpaulins, drip irrigation, and wire fencing
Access to latest weather reports, market prices (APMC), and agricultural advisories
Transparent application tracking and DBT processing

procedure: Visit the iKhedut portal (https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in)
Click on 'Yojana' (Schemes) and select the relevant category (Agriculture, Horticulture, Animal Husbandry, etc.)
Check if the application window is currently 'Open'
Fill the application form online; registration is optional but recommended
Take a printout, attach land/bank documents, and submit it to the Gram Sevak or Taluka office within 7 days
Pre-approval SMS is sent, after which purchase is made and final subsidy is transferred

name: Rythu Bandhu Scheme (Agriculture Investment Support Scheme)
description: A direct benefit transfer scheme by the Telangana Government providing investment support for agriculture and horticulture crops to relieve farmers from debt burdens.
authority: Department of Agriculture, Government of Telangana
eligibility: All land-owning farmers resident in Telangana
Applicable for both Kharif and Rabi seasons
Tenant farmers are generally excluded from direct cash transfer under this scheme
benefits: Direct grant of ₹5,000 per acre per season (Total ₹10,000 per acre per year)
Supports the purchase of inputs like seeds, fertilizers, pesticides, and labor
Amount is deposited directly into the farmer's bank account before the onset of the cropping season

procedure: Automatic inclusion based on digitized land records on the Dharani portal
New landowners or those missed out must approach the Village Revenue Officer (VRO) or Agricultural Extension Officer (AEO)
Submit a physical application with a copy of the new Pattadar passbook, Aadhaar, and bank details
Data is verified and updated in the central database, enabling automatic DBT for subsequent seasons

name: KALIA Scheme (Krushak Assistance for Livelihood and Income Augmentation)
description: A comprehensive state intervention for agricultural prosperity in Odisha, targeting small/marginal farmers, landless agricultural laborers, and vulnerable agricultural households.
authority: Department of Agriculture and Farmers' Empowerment, Govt of Odisha
eligibility: Small and Marginal Farmers (owning less than 5 acres of land)
Landless Agricultural Households
Vulnerable Agricultural Families (elderly, differently-abled, disease-stricken)
Must be a permanent resident of Odisha
benefits: Support for Cultivators: ₹4,000 per year per farm family (₹2,000 each for Kharif and Rabi), historically synchronized with PM-KISAN to ensure total ₹10,000 annual support
Livelihood Support for Landless: One-time grant of ₹12,500 for allied activities (goat rearing, poultry, mushroom cultivation)
Financial Assistance to Vulnerable: ₹10,000 per family per year for sustenance
Life insurance cover of ₹2 Lakh and accidental cover of ₹2 Lakh at highly subsidized premiums

procedure: Applications are accepted during specific registration drives or through the online KALIA portal
Farmers can apply by filling out the online form or depositing physical forms at the Gram Panchayat node
A draft list of beneficiaries is published at the Panchayat for social audit
Upon final approval, funds are transferred directly via DBT

name: YSR Rythu Bharosa - PM KISAN
description: An agriculture investment support scheme by the Government of Andhra Pradesh offering financial assistance to farmers, including tenant farmers, integrated with the PM-KISAN scheme.
authority: Department of Agriculture, Government of Andhra Pradesh
eligibility: Land-owning farming families in Andhra Pradesh
Landless Tenant Farmers and ROFR (Forest land) cultivators
Minimum cultivation of 1 acre required for tenant farmers (0.5 acre for vegetables/flowers)
benefits: Total financial assistance of ₹13,500 per farmer family per year
For landowners: ₹6,000 from PM-KISAN + ₹7,500 from State Government
For tenant farmers/ROFR cultivators: The entire ₹13,500 is provided by the State Government
Disbursed in three installments (May, October, and January/February)
documents: Crop Cultivator Rights Card (CCRC) for Tenant Farmers

procedure: Beneficiary identification is done at the Rythu Bharosa Kendras (RBKs) established in every village secretariat
Village Agriculture Assistant (VAA) conducts field verification
Tenant farmers must obtain a CCRC signed by the landowner and VRO
Verified lists are displayed at RBKs for social audit
Assistance is transferred directly to the Aadhaar-linked bank account

name: Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay SanraksHan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA)
description: An umbrella scheme to ensure remunerative prices to farmers for their produce, focusing primarily on pulses, oilseeds, and copra through robust procurement and price deficiency systems.
authority: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
eligibility: Farmers producing pulses, oilseeds, and copra in states implementing the scheme
Must be registered on the respective State procurement portals
benefits: Price Support Scheme (PSS): Physical procurement of pulses, oilseeds, and copra by Central Agencies (NAFED, FCI) at Minimum Support Price (MSP)
Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS): Direct payment of the difference between MSP and the selling/modal price without physical procurement (primarily for oilseeds)
Private Procurement & Stockist Scheme (PPSS): Participation of private sector in procurement operations at MSP
documents: Registration slip from State Procurement Portal

procedure: Farmers must register on the state-specific e-procurement portal (e.g., e-Uparjan, e-Kharid) during the specified window before harvest
Receive an SMS with the date to bring produce to the designated procurement center
For PSS: Produce is assayed and bought at MSP. Payment is credited via DBT
For PDPS: Farmer sells in the APMC mandi, and if the modal price is below MSP, the difference is paid via DBT

name: Kisan Suvidha Portal / App
description: An omnibus mobile app and web portal providing farmers with a single interface to access information on weather, market prices, seeds, fertilizers, machinery, and crop advisories.
authority: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
eligibility: All farmers and citizens
benefits: Single-point access to multiple agriculture schemes (PM-KISAN, PMFBY, Soil Health Card)
Real-time market price (mandi) tracking for crops within a 50 km radius
5-day weather forecasts and extreme weather alerts
Information on nearest dealers for seeds, fertilizers, and pesticides

procedure: Visit kisansuvidha.gov.in or download the Kisan Suvidha app from the UMANG platform / Play Store
Select language and enter mobile number
Click on desired modules (Weather, Market Price, PM-KISAN, etc.) to fetch real-time data directly

name: e-Urvarak (Fertilizer DBT Portal)
description: The national portal for the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system in fertilizers, tracking movement and sale of subsidized fertilizers to farmers.
authority: Department of Fertilizers, Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers
eligibility: Any farmer wishing to purchase subsidized fertilizers (Urea, DAP, NPK) from authorized retailers
benefits: Ensures availability of fertilizers at strictly subsidized MRP rates
Prevents diversion and black marketing of agricultural grade urea
Farmers can check fertilizer stock availability at retail shops in their district via the portal
documents: Aadhaar Card or KCC (Kisan Credit Card) or Voter ID (Required at the retail shop for biometric authentication)

procedure: Farmer visits the local authorized fertilizer retailer/cooperative society
Provides Aadhaar number and performs biometric fingerprint authentication on the Point of Sale (PoS) machine
Purchases the required quantity of fertilizer at subsidized rates
The subsidy amount is released directly to the fertilizer company by the Government post the sale transaction

name: Plant Quarantine Information System (PQIS)
description: A digital service facilitating the issuance of Phytosanitary Certificates for export and Import Permits for agricultural commodities to prevent the spread of exotic pests and diseases.
authority: Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine & Storage (DPPQS)
eligibility: Exporters and Importers of agricultural commodities, seeds, plants, and plant products
benefits: Online application and tracking of Phytosanitary Certificates (for export) and Import Permits
Ensures compliance with international SPS (Sanitary and Phytosanitary) agreements
Prevents delays at customs through digital integration with ICEGATE

procedure: Register on the PQMS (Plant Quarantine Management System) portal using IEC code
Submit an application for a Phytosanitary Certificate (Export) or Import Permit
Pay inspection/processing fees online
Officers conduct physical inspection and sampling of the consignment at the port/packhouse
If clear, the digital certificate is issued and sent to customs

name: Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) Knowledge Network
description: A portal connecting all Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) in the country to transfer agricultural technologies, conduct demonstrations, and provide direct expert interaction.
authority: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)
eligibility: All farmers seeking technological intervention, training, and modern farming techniques
benefits: Access to contact details of experts at the district-level KVK
Information on upcoming training programs, front-line demonstrations, and field days
Booking of soil/water testing services and purchasing improved seeds/saplings developed by ICAR
Access to package of practices for localized agro-climatic zones

procedure: Visit the KVK portal and select your State and District to find the local KVK
Farmers can view advisory boards and register for skill development training programs online
Farmers can physically visit the KVK to interact with scientists, test soil, and buy seeds

name: Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS)
description: An insurance scheme designed to mitigate the hardship of insured farmers against financial loss due to anticipated crop loss resulting from adverse weather conditions (rainfall, temperature, frost, humidity).
authority: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
eligibility: Farmers growing notified commercial and horticultural crops in notified areas
Voluntary for all farmers (loanee and non-loanee)
benefits: Insurance payout is triggered automatically based on weather data recorded at notified Reference Weather Stations (RWS), bypassing the need for individual crop cutting experiments (CCEs)
Covers risks like deficit rainfall, excess rainfall, unseasonal rainfall, high/low temperature, and frost
Low farmer premium rate (Max 5% for commercial/horticultural crops)

procedure: Operates alongside PMFBY on the same portal
Farmers apply on pmfby.gov.in or through bank branches / CSCs
Select the crop and check if it falls under RWBCIS in the respective district
Pay the premium share
Claims are calculated by the insurance company directly based on weather data from RWS and transferred via DBT

name: PMKSY - Har Khet Ko Pani (HKKP)
description: A component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana focusing on expanding cultivable area under assured irrigation, improving physical access of water on the farm, and groundwater development.
authority: Ministry of Jal Shakti / Ministry of Agriculture
eligibility: Individual farmers, groups of farmers, and Water User Associations (WUAs)
Applicable particularly in areas where groundwater development is less than 60% (Safe blocks)
benefits: Creation of new water sources through minor irrigation (both surface and groundwater)
Repair, restoration, and renovation of water bodies
Command Area Development and Water Management (CADWM)
Financial assistance for tube wells, bore wells, and dug wells in safe blocks
documents: Clearance from State Ground Water Authority (if required)
Project proposal / estimate from empanelled agency

procedure: Projects are usually aggregated at the Gram Panchayat / Block level to form a District Irrigation Plan (DIP)
Farmers apply to the Minor Irrigation Department or Agriculture Office of the state
Feasibility survey is conducted by hydrogeologists
Upon approval, funds are sanctioned for borewell/tubewell drilling or water body restoration

verification.notes: Verified from pmksy.gov.in HKKP operational guidelines.

name: National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm (NMEO-OP)
description: A centrally sponsored scheme to increase oil palm cultivation and boost domestic edible oil production, with special focus on the North East and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
authority: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
state: All India (Special focus on NER and A&N)
eligibility: Farmers owning land with assured irrigation facilities
Willing to grow Oil Palm over an extended gestation period (4-5 years)
benefits: Substantial assistance for planting material (up to ₹29,000 per ha)
Maintenance/cultivation cost assistance during gestation period (up to ₹21,000 per ha over 4 years)
Price Assurance mechanism (Viability Gap Payment) to protect farmers from global price volatility of Fresh Fruit Bunches (FFB)
Assistance for borewells, drip irrigation, and harvesting tools
documents: Agreement with partnered Oil Palm processing industry (MOU)

procedure: Farmers must approach the State Department of Agriculture/Horticulture or the designated Oil Palm processing company allotted to their mandate area
Sign an agreement for assured buy-back of FFB
Procure seedlings from authorized nurseries
Subsidy is released through DBT after joint inspection by state officials

name: Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Scheme (ACABC)
description: A scheme to tap the expertise of agricultural graduates to provide extension services to farmers while creating self-employment opportunities.
authority: Ministry of Agriculture / MANAGE / NABARD
eligibility: Graduates in agriculture and allied subjects from SAUs/Central Universities/ICAR recognized institutions
Diploma/Post Graduate Diploma holders in agriculture
Biological Science graduates with post-graduation in agriculture
benefits: Free 45-day residential training program on agri-entrepreneurship via MANAGE recognized Nodal Training Institutes (NTIs)
Bank loans available up to ₹20 Lakh (individual) and ₹100 Lakh (group of 5) for establishing Agri-Clinics/Agri-Business centers
Composite back-ended capital subsidy: 44% for SC/ST/Women/NER candidates and 36% for General category
documents: Detailed Project Report (DPR) for bank loan

procedure: Register online at agriclinics.net for the 45-day training program
Attend the training at the selected NTI and prepare a DPR
Submit the DPR to a commercial/cooperative bank for loan sanction
Once the loan is sanctioned and the project is established, NABARD releases the capital subsidy to the bank account

name: Krishi Megh
description: The National Agricultural Research & Education System-Cloud Infrastructure and Services, designed to protect digital data of ICAR and enhance digital agriculture services.
authority: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)
eligibility: ICAR institutes, State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), KVKs, and agricultural researchers/students
benefits: Provides robust and secure cloud infrastructure for agricultural research data
Hosts the KVK portal, e-Governance applications, and digital education platforms for agriculture students
Ensures business continuity and disaster recovery for agricultural research data across India

procedure: Agricultural institutions and universities integrate their digital services with Krishi Megh for hosting
Researchers and students access the hosted applications (like e-Krishi Shiksha) using institutional credentials
General public/farmers benefit indirectly through faster and resilient digital advisory services (like KVK portal) hosted on it

verification.notes: Verified from ICAR NAHEP Krishi Megh launch documents.
